reason: A compound of two inflorescence-form values, a panicle with a flat, corymb-like top. Both values exist, so it is a continuum or conjunction of corymb-like and panicle-like rather than a new term.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md, two qualities of one bearer: hemispheroid (PATO_0005000) and depressed (FLOPO:0991103)
reason: A hemisphere that is broader than high. Both qualities exist. Unlike depressed-globose (= oblate, rule C170), PATO has no single term for a flattened hemisphere.
'Petals disarticulate in fruit' means they are shed once the fruit forms: a shedability value plus a stage. PATO_0001506 diastatic (separated bones) is not the right term.
Drab is a dull, greyish or brownish, unsaturated colour. In 'royal blue, ± drab' it can only mean subdued. PATO lists 'pale' with low saturation, and FLOPO:0991363 sordid is the alternative.
The -ish suffix is read as 'approximately', as 'greenish' is (pattern 01). The value is dull.

target: docs/odp/07-alternatives.md over docs/odp/10-ratio-to-another-part.md (as long as) and docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (longer than), towards petal (PO_0009032)
reason: A comparison of length with another part, given as two alternatives. It is not a quality term.

target: docs/odp/07-alternatives.md over docs/odp/10-ratio-to-another-part.md and docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md, towards perigynium (PO_0009044)
reason: The same comparison as 'equal to or exceeding petals', with the perigynium as the second term.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md, two qualities of the trichome: bifurcated (PATO_0001784) and stipitate (FLOPO:0991065)
reason: A stalked hair that forks at the top, as in Brassicaceae. It is a compound of two existing values, so it needs no term.
A vague simile ('like a gullet') for the lip blade, found in one construction. Its meaning (throat-like, open, tubular) is too uncertain to map or to define.
'Leaf scars half round' = shaped like a half circle. PATO lists 'half circle' as a synonym of semicircular.
Hairs between hispidulous and strigillose (= strigulose). Both values exist, so it is a two-value compound.
Deltate = triangular (PATO_0001875 has the synonym deltoid). PATO already has the compound shape lanceolate-triangular.
The colour table lists 'chestnut', 'chestnut brown' and 'light chestnut' as NARROW synonyms of reddish brown. 'Light' is a degree modifier.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md: trichome (PO_0000282) of the petiole/leaf lamina + sparse (PATO_0001609); 'long' as the state of the hairs (docs/odp/04-state-of-the-bearer.md)
reason: A transcription where part and quality were fused. The bearer is the hairs of the organ and the quality is their density. 'Sparse to common' is a continuum.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md: surrounding (PATO_0001772) towards the fruit or achene, with 'loosely' as qualifier
reason: 'Calyx loosely enclosing the berry' relates the calyx to another part. The relational term exists (PATO lists 'enclosing' as a synonym of surrounding).
A plain negation of an existing PATO shape.
'Leaf blade not folding' denies the folded state, for example a blade that stays flat rather than folding at night or when touched.

'Margins obscurely differentiated' and 'claw obscurely differentiated' mean the part is not clearly set off. This follows rule C174 (obscure → inconspicuous). PATO_0002106 poorly differentiated is a cellular/pathology term.
A pseudopedate leaf looks pedate and differs only in how it develops, which a flora phenotype does not record. The visible form is pedate.
'Scarcely' reverses the sense of 'gaping' (the part is nearly closed). The bearers differ (corolla mouth, leaf sheath), and mapping to PATO_0000610 open would misstate the text.

label: turpentine-scented
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having a sharp, resinous odour like that of turpentine.
reason: A distinct, diagnostic odour (Pinaceae, Anacardiaceae, Burseraceae) that the existing scent classes do not cover. It is a sibling of FLOPO:0991017 spicy-scented and FLOPO:0991019 sour-smelling.
The word is ambiguous between 'bladder-like, inflated' (scale) and the Spanish 'roseta utricular' (a water-holding tank rosette). With 4 statements, no single reading is safe.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md, two qualities of the margin (FLOPO_0986053): velutinous (PATO_0104041) and ciliate (the pipeline's grounding for 'ciliate')
reason: A margin that is velvety and fringed with hairs, a compound of two existing values. Do not use PATO_0001408 ciliated, which refers to cell cilia.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md, two qualities of one bearer: angular (PATO_0001977) and flattened (PATO_0002254)
reason: A compound of two existing values. Do not use PATO_0001485 condensed, whose synonym 'compressed' is a pathology sense.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum): obtuse (PATO_0001935) – truncated (PATO_0000936), bearer leaf lamina base (PO_0008019)
reason: A part with a two-value compound: the blade base lies between rounded and truncate. Both values exist.

target: docs/odp/17-value-defined-by-a-measure.md: relative position of the widest point (FLOPO:0995011) ≥ 0.6
reason: It states where the blade is widest without saying its length:width ratio or outline, so it implies neither obovate nor oblanceolate. Pattern 17's widest-point measure says exactly this.

target: new: coloured marking — streaked (FLOPO:0991206) with brown (PATO_0000952) as the colour of the streaks
reason: A compound of a pattern value and the colour of the marks. Streaked exists, and the colour belongs to the streaks, not to the whole part.
A relation to a named second part. PATO's relational 'surrounded by' (synonym 'enclosed by') fits it exactly. It often alternates with 'exserted' (pattern 07).
'Phyllary tips hair-tufted' = a tuft of hairs at one end, which is exactly comose. 'Tips' is the location of the tuft.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md: plant organ apex (FLOPO_0985023) of the phyllary/sepal + herbaceous texture
reason: A part (the tip) and a texture value, as against scarious phyllaries. Note that PATO_0002352 herbaceous is defined as dying back to the rootstock, so 'herbaceous' as a green, leaf-like texture still has no correct term.
